title: Drift and Hotpatch Tactical Log
content:
Quick log for thinking through small/cohort canaries plus emergency hotpatch flow focused on model drift signals. Rough, unpolished — todo list + watchlist for next few releases.

Context / why this exists
- We've seen subtle output drift in a handful of tenants over the last 2 quarters; not catastrophic but increases hallucination-rate and customer tickets. Need a lightweight, repeatable on-call + eng flow that combines automated drift detection with a safe hotpatch path.
- Goal: detect meaningful semantic drift early, quarantine affected cohort(s), and ship a targeted hotpatch (config/weight pin/short rollback) inside 60–90 minutes when safe.

Definitions / quick signal list (what to watch)
- Semantic drift (embedding shift): rolling-window cosine distance between 1k cached prompts' embeddings vs baseline > 0.08 for 1h -> noisy but actionable.
- KL-ish token distribution shift: per-model token unigram distribution shift > 3 sigma over 6h window.
- Quality-eval regression: synthetic eval set (30 prompts) drop in rubric score >= 5 points vs baseline (daily run).
- Hallucination proxy: external fact-checker mismatch rate increase > 1.5x baseline (hourly cadence).
- Latency and cost: p95 latency up 30% + tokens-per-call increase > 20% (suggests output length blowup).
- Error surge: 5xx rate > 0.2% for > 10m.

Alert tiers and actions
- Tier A (Immediate): quality-eval regression + hallucination spike OR embedding cosine > 0.1 for 2 consecutive checks. -> Notify #eng-hotpatch + paging SRE. Start hotpatch pipeline.
- Tier B (Watch): token distribution shift or latency spike alone -> put traffic in warmdown window, increase telemetry sampling, bump canary partition to 0% for at-risk cohorts if configured.

Canary progression plan (default template)
- Preflight: small eval run vs smoke prompt set (10 prompts) within last 24h, KV cache priming on canary nodes.
- Step 0 (priming): route 0.5% traffic for 30m (or 1000 requests whichever first). Collect p50/p95 latency, avg tokens, hallucination proxy sampling.
- Step 1: 1% for 45m. Check: eval set stable, embedding shift < 0.04, error < 0.05%.
- Step 2: 5% for 60m. Check: no Tier A signals, client error budget OK.
- Step 3: 20% for 2h. If stable, increase to 50% then 100% over next 6–12h depending on risk profile.
- Deviation rule: Any Tier A signal -> immediate step back to previous stable fraction and escalate.

Cohort pinning rules (tenant-specific)
- Critical tenants (SLA): default pinned to previously validated model version unless explicitly approved for roll.
- Non-critical / self-serve tenants: opt-in for early canaries; default to global rollout after 24h stable at 20%
- Pin metadata should include: model-hash, quantization-profile, kernel-set, serving-image-tag. Keep pin records for 90 days.

Hotpatch flow (emergency small-fix path)
- Trigger: Tier A alert OR customer-facing outage/incorrect-behavior high severity ticket.
- Owner: on-call eng lead + SRE contact. Slack: @oncall-sre + #eng-hotpatch.
- Steps (fast lane):
  1) Quarantine: divert suspect traffic to fallback model variant (compatible smaller model) via routing policy. Drop suspect tenant fraction to 0% on new variant nodes.
  2) Quick mitigation (if config-only): toggle local prompt-sanitizer / decoding knobs via runtime feature-flag. Test on smoke set (5 prompts).
  3) If code/weights needed: build hotpatch image (builder-image-hotpatch-<timestamp>), run smoke container on staging, sanity eval, then promote to warmpool nodes for canary.
  4) If fix validated: promote to remaining canary steps. If not validated -> rollback to pinned version and record incident.
- Time budget targets: quarantine step < 10m, mitigation toggle < 20m, image build + smoke < 45–90m depending on infra load.

Telemetry to collect (minimal necessary)
- Per-tenant: p50/p95 latency, call-rate, avg tokens, 5xx rate, embedding-cosine-sample, hallucination-proxy-rate, user-reported tickets (ingested).
- Per-model: top tokens distribution deltas, KV cache hit ratio, GPU util, batching efficiency, sequence length distribution.
- Sampling controls: increase prompt-level sampling weight from 1% -> 10% during canary to get better coverage.

Runbook snippets (notes to self)
- When toggling fallback routing, remember to set sticky-cookie TTL = 2h to avoid cold-start churn for affected cohorts.
- Warmup KV cache: replay 2k most common prefixes from production cache if available; otherwise run synthetic priming script (scripts/primers/kv_warmup.sh).
- If hallucination proxy increases but embedding shift is low, suspect prompt template change; check feature flags or client SDK updates in last 24h.

Communication checklist
- Immediate: post alert summary to #eng-hotpatch + create JIRA ticket with "hotpatch" label.
- If customer-facing: notify CS lead (Lena Ortiz) and send short incident note to account owner within 30–60m.
- Postmortem: link to incident page, note what signals fired and timeline, propose long-term fix.

Open TODOs / ideas to tighten detection
- Build a lightweight rolling shadow-eval that runs on a small set of recently seen prompts per tenant (helps detect client-specific drift earlier).
- Add an embedding-cluster outlier detector to catch narrow-domain degradation (e.g., for tenant A where query distribution shifts).
- Automate a quick binary search traffic shift tool: when a Tier A is detected, run automated shrink/expand steps to find safe fraction in 15–30m.

Notes (random)
- Keep hotpatch image tags descriptive: hotpatch-<jira>-<git-sha>-<timestamp>.
- We should baseline embedding cosine noise floor per model per region; current thresholds feel global and too blunt.

Immediate action items (for next on-call)
- Omar: add embedding sampling to hourly pipeline (small job) -> aim for +1 sampling point per tenant.
- Lena: draft short email template for notifying customers of canary-related regressions.
- Me (Tara): prototype the auto-shrink traffic script; aim for MVP before next major release.

Scratchpad thoughts (bullet-y)
- Could we use a synthetic semantic-check that verifies named-entity stability? Maybe cheaper than full eval.
- Hotpatches should prefer config changes first (lower risk).
- Need a better way to store per-tenant pinned metadata (lightweight KV store with audit trail).

-- end of notes --

Revision history: rough timeline of edits
- 2025-11-02 initial draft
- 2025-12-10 added canary progression template
- 2026-02-28 expanded telemetry + hotpatch time budgets
